institution: Uttar Pradesh University of Medical Sciences, Saifai (Department of Microbiology)
citation: Department of Microbiology, Uttar Pradesh University of Medical Sciences. Antibiogram (based on clinical isolates from UPUMS Hospital), January 2024 to December 2024. Saifai, Etawah: UPUMS; 2025.
reporting: Percent susceptible by specimen (urine, blood, respiratory, pus and other exudates, sterile body fluids) and organism, hospital-wide, with the number of isolates per organism; each table is repeated as a labelled bar chart. Sample counts by ICU, ward and OPD and organism distributions (per cent) are given per specimen, but the susceptibility tables are not split by setting. AST method and breakpoint standard not stated.

verification.note: All 33 'Presentation of antibiogram' tables parsed from the PDF text layer (header cells decoded from rotated text; each value assigned to its column by x-position) and compared value by value, with each row's organism and isolate number, against crops of the rendered pages (scale 2.4); all 365 cells and 33 n values agree.

notes: Hospital antibiogram of UPUMS Saifai for January to December 2024 (67 pages). Per specimen the document gives the samples received from ICU, wards and OPD (urine 1480/1950/1659, blood 4855/1905/42, respiratory 700/380/662, pus 475/1215/950, sterile body fluids 514/1230/92), culture positivity, the bacteriological profile (per cent) overall and by department, and one percent-susceptible table per organism with its isolate number. The susceptibility tables are hospital-wide, so every row is recorded as all settings. Sterile body fluids include CSF, gastric aspirate and vitreous fluid as listed on p4; respiratory samples include throat swabs. Two pairs of tables print identical percentages for every drug although their isolate numbers differ (respiratory and pus Pseudomonas; pus and sterile body fluid S. aureus), which suggests a copy error in the source; they are recorded as printed with a note. Blood Staphylococcus and Candida species tables (pp27 and 29) agree with the antibiogram isolate numbers (S. aureus 534; CoNS species 310 in all; Candida species 113 in all). No isolate count table by specimen and setting is printed, so no counts are recorded. Bar charts repeat the table values and were used as a cross-check, except on p24 (blood Acinetobacter: chart ceftriaxone 75% and tigecycline 98% against the table's 64% and 100%) and p61 (sterile body fluid S. aureus: chart differs from the table for 8 of 9 drugs); those figures carry conflict entries. Page numbers are PDF pages (printed page number plus 1).
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 365 cells (the seeded 40% sample of 146 plus every other cell) and all 33 row n values re-read against the page images (scale 2.2, crops at scale 3.5), each value read before comparing, and every table also compared with the data labels of its own bar chart; 0 transcription errors, no value changed.

Two source inconsistencies the extraction had not recorded are now conflict entries (table values kept): p24 blood Acinetobacter, the chart labels ceftriaxone 75% and tigecycline 98% against the table's 64% and 100%; p61 sterile body fluid S. aureus, the table repeats the pus S. aureus table (p50) exactly while the page's own chart differs for 8 of 9 drugs and the printed MSSA share (17 of 30, 57%) matches the chart's cefoxitin 57%, so the p61 table is probably a copy error. The notes' statement that all charts repeat their tables is corrected.

Confirmed as printed: respiratory (n=125, p40) and pus (n=107, p49) Pseudomonas give identical figures for all 11 drugs in both table and chart; the 6 caution cells (K. oxytoca urine and Citrobacter sterile tigecycline 98% with n=30, Acinetobacter respiratory tigecycline 98% with n=33, Acinetobacter blood cefepime, imipenem and ciprofloxacin 68% with n=13) and the 4 intrinsic Acinetobacter ertapenem cells are printed as recorded; so are the 5 urinary tigecycline cells the build now hides (E. coli 95%, K. pneumoniae 98%, K. oxytoca 98%, Citrobacter 94%, Acinetobacter 98%).
